l4_steps.name: Receive and log corporate RFP in CRM
l4_steps.input: RFP document from corporate travel manager or TMC (BCD, Amex GBT, CWT)
l4_steps.output: Logged account record with RFP details, TMC affiliation, and route footprint
l4_steps.kpi: RFP acknowledged within 2 business days; 100% of RFPs logged before pricing work begins
l4_steps.pain_point: RFPs arriving via TMC intermediaries create version-control conflicts when the corporate client also engages the airline directly, leading to duplicate records in Salesforce

l4_steps.name: Assess historical travel volume and route fit
l4_steps.input: Account travel history, O&D booking data from Sabre PRISM, prior contract performance (if renewal)
l4_steps.output: Volume assessment report with top-10 O&Ds, revenue contribution, and route coverage score
l4_steps.kpi: Minimum qualifying annual spend $250K; route overlap ≥60% of account top-10 O&Ds
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST O&D data attributes bookings to agency PCC rather than corporate ID, making true account volume difficult to isolate without PRISM reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Determine account tier and eligibility decision
l4_steps.input: Volume assessment report, account strategic value flags
l4_steps.output: Tier assignment (Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3) or formal decline notification
l4_steps.kpi: ≥95% of eligible accounts tiered within 2 business days of volume assessment
l4_steps.pain_point: Tier thresholds are static annual targets and do not account for seasonal concentration; high-value accounts with strong Q4 travel patterns may be under-tiered mid-year

l4_steps.name: Model discount scenarios by O&D and cabin
l4_steps.input: Tier assignment, baseline fare inventory by booking class, O&D demand curves from SkyCAST
l4_steps.output: Discount scenario matrix (3–5 discount options per cabin class per contracted O&D)
l4_steps.kpi: Modelled revenue dilution <3% vs unconstrained network revenue on contracted routes
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus NRM inventory controls on high-demand routes may cap discount depth without manual override by the Revenue Manager, creating tension between corporate sales targets and RM policy

l4_steps.name: Validate discount against yield floor — gate
l4_steps.input: Discount scenario matrix, route-level yield floor thresholds
l4_steps.output: Approved discount bands per O&D; rejected scenarios returned for rework
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue dilution from corporate contract ≤2% on constrained routes; ≤5% on off-peak routes
l4_steps.pain_point: Yield floors are set seasonally and may not reflect intra-season demand shifts; approving discounts in low-demand periods can conflict with late-breaking demand spikes not yet captured in SkyCAST forecasts

l4_steps.name: Draft and issue corporate pricing proposal
l4_steps.input: Approved discount bands, account tier, standard contract terms template
l4_steps.output: Formal pricing proposal document with fare basis codes, discount levels, and volume commitments
l4_steps.kpi: Proposal issued within 3 business days of yield approval; 100% of proposals include ATPCO-compatible fare basis code references
l4_steps.pain_point: Proposal templates are maintained separately from ATPCO rule structures; manual reconciliation is needed before filing, introducing errors when templates are not updated after ATPCO rule changes

l4_steps.name: Negotiate terms with corporate client or TMC
l4_steps.input: Pricing proposal, client travel policy requirements, TMC contracting requirements
l4_steps.output: Negotiation log with revised terms, version-controlled counter-proposal
l4_steps.kpi: Negotiation cycle completed in ≤3 rounds; average cycle time ≤10 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: TMC-represented clients (BCD, Amex GBT) frequently introduce non-standard contract clauses (guaranteed availability, cap-on-surcharges) outside the airline's standard ATPCO framework, requiring legal review that extends cycle time

l4_steps.name: Assess commercial impact of counter-proposal
l4_steps.input: Client counter-proposal terms, updated O&D volume commitment data
l4_steps.output: Updated revenue impact model with go/no-go recommendation
l4_steps.kpi: Counter-proposal modelled and responded to within 1 business day
l4_steps.pain_point: Frequent counter-proposals on routes shared with alliance partners or interline agreements require additional proration impact analysis not automated in NRM, adding 2–3 days to cycle time

l4_steps.name: Obtain pricing committee sign-off
l4_steps.input: Final negotiated terms, revenue impact model, legal review outcome
l4_steps.output: Signed approval record with contract reference number
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of contracts with annual value >$1M approved at VP level; approval latency ≤2 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Approval workflows are largely email-based with no enforced audit trail in Salesforce; negotiated terms can deviate from the approved scenario without detection, creating post-execution disputes

l4_steps.name: File negotiated fares in ATPCO (Cat-15)
l4_steps.input: Approved contract terms, fare basis codes, routing rules, advance-purchase conditions
l4_steps.output: ATPCO-filed private fares with Category 15 (Accompanied Travel) or Category 25 (Fare By Rule) entries
l4_steps.kpi: Fare filing completed ≥2 business days before contract effective date; 0% mis-pricing incidents on go-live day
l4_steps.pain_point: Category 15 private fare rule coding errors (incorrect routing restrictions or permitted combinations) surface only at booking engine pricing, causing customer-facing mis-pricing and requiring urgent ATPCO re-filing

l4_steps.name: Load and activate private fares in PSS
l4_steps.input: ATPCO-filed fare reference, booking class allocation, contract effective dates
l4_steps.output: Fare basis codes activated in Altéa inventory with correct booking class and date validity
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of contracted fare basis codes active in PSS ≥24 hours before go-live; zero booking-class mismatches
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS fare activation requires a manual QA step by a separate Revenue Management team; handoff gaps between Tariff and RM teams cause last-minute activation failures discovered only when test bookings are attempted

l4_steps.name: Configure corporate access in distribution channels
l4_steps.input: Contract activation record, corporate account code, TMC GDS subscriber IDs
l4_steps.output: Corporate account code active in NDC, Sabre GDS, Travelport GDS, and direct booking channels
l4_steps.kpi: Corporate traveller can book contracted fare within 24 hours of go-live; NDC channel coverage ≥80% of contracted fare conditions
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API Gateway does not support all Category 15 private fare rule conditions (e.g. negotiated blackout dates); non-compliant fares fall back to GDS-only distribution, limiting direct channel adoption targets

l4_steps.name: Validate end-to-end booking flow — gate
l4_steps.input: Test PNRs across all contracted O&Ds, channels (GDS, NDC, direct), and cabin classes
l4_steps.output: Booking validation report; confirmed go-live sign-off or defect list for remediation
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of test bookings price correctly across all channels before live date; defects remediated within 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS test environment does not always replicate live Altéa inventory state; a clean test result can still produce pricing failures in production if RM inventory availability differs from the test snapshot

l4_steps.name: Monitor monthly volume commitment attainment
l4_steps.input: Monthly booking data from Sabre PRISM, direct and NDC booking feeds, contract volume schedule
l4_steps.output: Monthly volume attainment dashboard with trajectory vs annual commitment
l4_steps.kpi: Volume reporting latency ≤3 business days after month-end; attainment variance flagged if >10% below commitment trajectory
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre PRISM captures GDS-originated bookings only; direct channel and NDC bookings require separate reconciliation from Altéa PSS, causing systematic under-reporting of attainment and triggering false at-risk alerts

l4_steps.name: Identify and intervene on at-risk accounts
l4_steps.input: Monthly volume attainment dashboard, account-level booking trend analysis from AWS Redshift
l4_steps.output: At-risk account list with root-cause annotation and recommended intervention actions
l4_steps.kpi: ≥80% of accounts on-track to meet annual commitment by month 6; at-risk accounts contacted within 5 business days of flag
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau dashboards are refreshed from AWS Redshift nightly; intra-month booking surges or drops are invisible until the next refresh cycle, delaying intervention and jeopardising end-of-year rebate qualification

l4_steps.name: Calculate and process annual rebates
l4_steps.input: Final annual volume attainment data, contract rebate tier schedule, reconciled booking records
l4_steps.output: Rebate payment or credit note issued to corporate account
l4_steps.kpi: Rebate processed within 30 days of contract year-end; 100% of rebate calculations independently verified against PRISM and Altéa data
l4_steps.pain_point: Rebate calculations depend on reconciled volume data across PRISM (GDS), Altéa PSS (direct/NDC), and SAP AR; discrepancies between sources cause disputes that delay payment and damage account relationships

l4_steps.name: Conduct annual contract performance review
l4_steps.input: Full-year performance scorecard, market rate benchmarks, account strategic value assessment
l4_steps.output: Contract performance scorecard with renewal recommendation and proposed revised terms
l4_steps.kpi: Review initiated ≥90 days before contract expiry; 100% of Tier 1 accounts reviewed in person
l4_steps.pain_point: Account managers carrying portfolios of >50 corporate contracts lack automated renewal-pipeline visibility in Salesforce; late review initiation (within 30 days of expiry) forces rushed renegotiation and weakens the airline's commercial position

l4_steps.name: Trigger renewal, renegotiation, or termination
l4_steps.input: Contract performance scorecard, renewal recommendation, updated market discount benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Renewal instruction (loops back to Phase 2) or notice of termination issued to account
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of contracts actioned ≥60 days before expiry; zero contracts lapsing without a documented decision
l4_steps.pain_point: Accounts flagged for termination due to low volume often have strategic route dependencies (e.g. government contracts on thin markets) that override commercial logic; no system-enforced escalation path exists to flag strategic override decisions for VP review
